nodes.label: RMI 368X Electra-Piano
nodes.copy:
Every RMI 368X we restore for sale goes through the same meticulous process we're known for, with dozens of hours devoted to bringing each instrument to exceptional playing condition. We prioritize period-correct vintage components whenever possible, and turn to the best available reproduction parts when originals are no longer viable — always working to preserve the instrument's original character and tone. The result is an instrument that plays and sounds better than it likely has in decades.

The Electra-Piano was the flagship electronic keyboard from Rocky Mount Instruments (RMI), a subsidiary of the Allen Organ Company based in Rocky Mount, North Carolina, active from 1966 to 1982. The 368X, introduced in 1974, is the 68-key version of RMI's 300 Series Electra-Piano/Harpsichord and became a fixture of 1970s progressive rock — used extensively by Rick Wakeman (Yes), Tony Banks (Genesis), and Don Preston (The Mothers of Invention), among others. It layers piano, harpsichord, and lute-toned voices together with an accent/percussion effect and an organ-style sustain mode, all packed into an 85-pound capsule with folding legs for easy transport.

Features:
- Cleaned, Lubricated & Restored Key Contacts and Switches
- Addressed Transistor Drift for Stable, In-Tune Voicing
- New Electrolytic Capacitors
- Fully Restored Power Supply
- CEPCo's Expert Tuning & Voicing Setup
- Cleaned All Switches & Connectors
- All Voltages Checked & Calibrated for Optimum Performance
- New Cables

Included:
- Folding Legs
